reason: The sole in-scope claim (c1: that the A&S five-coefficient composition's Phi error multiplied by |x| exceeds the 1e-6 absolute tolerance at moderate |x|=4-10) was rebutted by an exhaustive runtime probe. The probe swept all 63,488 finite FP16 values — the complete legal input domain defined by problem.txt ("EVERY finite FP16 value is legal") — through the kernel on T4 CUDA and compared against the kernel's own FP64 erfc reference. Max absolute error was 5.27e-7 (worst input ~0.91), with 0 of 63,488 values exceeding the 1e-6 tolerance; targeted moderate inputs ±4..±10 showed errors at most 1.54e-7. Since the contract requires only abs(actual - GELU(x)) <= 1e-6 for every finite FP16 input and explicitly permits polynomial/rational approximations meeting that tolerance, this domain-exhaustive evidence confirms compliance. The contract's explicit approximation allowance (problem.txt: "Polynomial, rational, tanh or other approximations are permitted if they satisfy this fixed absolute tolerance throughout the entire legal domain") makes the small approximation error acceptable. All claims have evidence, the Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and recorded no new claims, and no open claims remain.
